A Critique of Political Economy

Published in 1849, A Critique of Political Economy is a foundational theoretical text by Karl Marx that critiques the economic systems of capitalism and their effects on society. The work presents Marx's key ideas about alienation, exploitation, and the labor theory of value.

Marx's critique was influenced by the writings of Adam Smith and other classical economists, but it also challenged the dominant ideologies of his time.

A Critique of Political Economy has had a profound impact on modern economic thought and continues to influence contemporary debates about capitalism, socialism, and economic inequality.

"The labor theory of value is the true basis of all economic phenomena," Marx wrote in the book. "The whole world is involved in this struggle." The critique's legacy can be seen in the rise of socialist movements and the ongoing debate about the role of government in regulating the economy.
